Goal: I can prove properties of isosceles trapezoids and kites.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Under this course's inclusive trapezoid convention, define an isosceles trapezoid relative to a chosen base pair by congruent base angles, equivalently reflection symmetry exchanging the base endpoints. Rectangles count; oblique parallelograms do not.

Theorem: the base angles of an isosceles trapezoid are equal, and its diagonals are equal.

Theorem: the diagonals of a kite are perpendicular, and one diagonal (the one joining the vertices between the equal sides) bisects the other.

Proof (kite): with AB = AD and CB = CD, triangle ABC is congruent to triangle ADC by SSS, so AC bisects angles A and C. Then SAS on the small triangles at the diagonal crossing gives equal right angles.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: A kite has diagonals of 10 and 16, with the 16 cm diagonal bisected. Are the diagonals perpendicular?
slides.reveal: Yes. The diagonals of a kite are always perpendicular.

slides.title: Common mistake
slides.html:
A student says: All trapezoids are isosceles.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.
